## Working Papers

<!-- NOTE: JMP designation confirmed as Jean's preference. Verify with Haliassos before publishing. -->

::: {.paper}
[**Branches and Roots: Banking Presence and Deforestation in Amazonian Indigenous Lands**]{.paper-title} <!-- [Job Market Paper]{.jmp-label} -->

[With Douglas K.G. de Araujo]{.paper-authors}

[Indigenous lands shelter much of the Brazilian Amazon's intact forest, yet illegal deforestation inside their boundaries has been climbing despite formal legal protection. We exploit a sharp expansion and subsequent contraction of the region's bank-branch network between 2008 and 2024 to ask whether local banking presence affects deforestation inside nearby Indigenous lands. We find that each additional branch near an Indigenous land lowers cumulative forest loss inside that area by roughly 2.5 km² over five years. Mediation analysis attributes the bulk of this effect to a single channel: bank presence raises local social capital, and exogenous variation in social capital in turn lowers deforestation. By contrast, we find no evidence that either local economic conditions or access to capital for clearing transmits the effect.]{.paper-summary}

[PDF *(coming soon)*]{.paper-btn .paper-btn--pdf} [Interactive Online Appendix](appendix-branches-and-roots/){.paper-btn}
:::

::: {.paper}
[**Actual and Perceived Financial Knowledge over the Life Cycle**]{.paper-title}

[What happens when households believe they know more than they actually do about financial matters? I use causal evidence to show that overconfidence leads households to drain their retirement savings early, fall behind on their mortgages, and lean too heavily on credit cards. A calibrated life-cycle model then traces how the damage compounds across the working years and lands hardest in the retirement years.]{.paper-summary}

[PDF](papers/actual-perceived-financial-knowledge.pdf){.paper-btn .paper-btn--pdf}
:::
